title: Amihan Wind

blocks.text: Tax is ignored: the project benefits from an income tax holiday.

Luzon needs every megawatt of clean power it can get, and spot prices on the wholesale market have risen for three years in a row. We will re-contract at the same level or better. Our solar portfolio was financed over 18 years by two other banks; we expect the same here.
The sponsor's base case uses our P90. We have no concerns on the yield.

The selected turbine is certified for typhoon-class winds (IEC class T) and has more than ten years of operating history in Taiwan and Japan. Insurance quotes include typhoon damage and business interruption.

The full-service agreement covers the first 5 years of operation, including the manufacturer's warranty and a 97% availability guarantee. The USD 1.8m per year in the business plan reflects that price. From year 6, once the warranty ends, we estimate USD 3.0m per year for a comparable scope: scheduled and unscheduled maintenance, major component replacement and higher insurance premiums.

items: Plant design, EPC contract and grid connection: sound, no concerns.

onStart.text: Hi, Amihan is Northpoint's first wind project and they want to bring us their whole Luzon pipeline if this goes well. Their solar portfolio got 18 years elsewhere, so they expect the same from us. Term sheet by Friday, and please keep the documentation light, they found our last requests heavy.

committeeClosing.text: Thank you. The committee will deliberate. You'll hear from us shortly.

conditions.reason: Covers Silverbay (25%, indirect, no identified owner). Required before signing, it does not stop the approval.

conditions.label: Higher margin (+50 bp)
conditions.reason: More revenue for the bank, but a higher rate raises debt service and makes every DSCR worse.

committee.question: What happens to the cash flows after year 12, and how did you size the tenor?
committee.goodAnswer: The PPA ends in year 12; after that the plant sells at merchant prices, 6.0 cents in the market study's low case, not 7.6. Over 18 years the DSCR would fall to 0.99x against a 1.50x requirement. A 12-year tenor removes the merchant tail and supports USD 58m.

ideas.label: The PPA ends in year 12, merchant prices after
The sponsor's price is too high: the market study's low case

committee.question: Are the operating costs in the business plan realistic for the whole life of the loan?
committee.goodAnswer: No: USD 1.8m only covers the 5-year warranty period. The engineer expects USD 3.0m from year 6, which brings the cash flow down to USD 9.78m and the maximum debt to USD 58m.

ideas.label: Impact on the cash flow or the debt size

committee.question: Can we hold this loan on our balance sheet?
committee.goodAnswer: Not all of it: the loan counts against the offtaker's group, with USD 155m used out of a USD 200m limit, so USD 45m available. Hold USD 45m and syndicate the rest, or lend less.

ideas.label: Hold part and syndicate, or lend less

committee.question: Northpoint is unhappy with our document requests. Can we keep it simple to close by Friday?
committee.goodAnswer: No on KYC: a 25% shareholder in the British Virgin Islands has no identified beneficial owner, and full KYC above 10% is required before signing. It does not block the approval; offer to help them provide it quickly. Firm but constructive.

weak.story: The debt is sized outside policy on the bank case. Year 6 brings the cost step-up, the merchant tail looms, and the loan goes on the watchlist.

compliance.label: Blocked by Compliance

outcomeContext: The consequence appears a few cases later, when the O&M contract comes up for renewal.

spotted: The PPA ends after 12 years, but the loan runs 18. The sponsor assumed the same price forever; the market study's low case is 6.0 cents, and policy requires 1.50x on merchant revenues. Over 18 years the DSCR falls to 0.99x from year 13.
The USD 1.8m of operating costs only covers the 5-year warranty. From year 6 the engineer expects USD 3.0m.
The loan counts against the offtaker's group limit: only USD 45m is available, whatever the DSCR.
A 25% shareholder in the British Virgin Islands has no identified owner. KYC on the listed parent does not cover it.
debrief.summary: The fix: a 12-year tenor (which supports more debt, USD 58m, than 18 years), the bank's share capped at USD 45m with the rest syndicated, and full KYC before signing.
debrief.lesson: A good project is not automatically a good loan. Look at the whole life of the debt, and at the whole bank.

answerKey.summary: The project is sound in its first years, but the sponsor's case hides two step-downs in cash flow, and two bank-side constraints apply whatever the DSCR. As requested (USD 69.75m over 18 years), the deal fails all four tests.

traps.title: Trap 1 — PPA shorter than the debt
traps.text: The PPA runs 12 years, the loan 18. The sponsor assumes the same 7.6 cents after year 12. The market study's low case, recommended for lenders, is 6.0 cents from the mid-2030s. On the bank case, the DSCR falls to 0.99x from year 13, and policy requires 1.50x on merchant revenues. Cutting the tenor to 12 years removes the merchant tail: the bank can then lend more (USD 58.2m) than over 18 years (USD 45.9m).

traps.title: Trap 2 — Operating costs after the warranty
traps.text: The USD 1.8m per year only holds for the 5-year full-service agreement. The engineer expects USD 3.0m from year 6. On its own the trap is discreet (DSCR 1.36x from year 6 at USD 69.75m), but it cuts the maximum debt over 12 years from USD 65.3m to USD 58.2m.

traps.title: Trap 3 — Single-group exposure
traps.text: The loan counts against the offtaker's group limit: USD 45m available. The bank can hold at most USD 45m, whatever the DSCR. The rest must be syndicated to another bank, or the loan reduced.

traps.title: Trap 4 — Incomplete KYC
traps.text: A 25% indirect shareholder (Silverbay, British Virgin Islands) has no identified beneficial owner. KYC on the listed parent alone does not cover it. Full KYC on all direct and indirect shareholders above 10% must be a condition before signing. It does not stop the approval, only the signing.

rightDecision.title: Right decision: approve with conditions
options: Debt sized within policy on the bank case: USD 58.2m at most over 12 years (best for the client), or USD 45.9m at most over 18 years (acceptable). Over 12 years at USD 58m: debt service USD 7.50m, DSCR 1.30x, gearing 62%, sponsor equity USD 35.0m.
The bank's share capped at USD 45m: syndicate the rest, or lend USD 45m only.
Full KYC on all direct and indirect shareholders above 10% before signing.

answerKey.extraCredit: Conditions that earn extra credit: the 6-month DSRA funded at close (about USD 3.8m at USD 58m over 12 years) and a dividend lock-up below 1.20x DSCR.
answerKey.weakAnswers: Weak answers: an 18-year loan sized on the sponsor's prices, a PPA extension the sponsor cannot deliver, a higher margin, or declining because of the KYC request (the right move is to require it, not to walk away).
